subject: Eval success signals: sprint milestones, tie-breakers, and rollback plan
messages:

Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval MAP + critical acceptance questions

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we discussed, our leadership wants a short mutual action plan that ties technical acceptance tests to go/no-go decisions for the pilot. Two asks up front:

1) Can you outline concrete success signals we can measure during the 4-week pilot (not just vague "accuracy")?
2) We need explicit rollback/exit gates and the exact evidence we'll require to sign off.

I've attached our discovery notes; procurement will also need a retention/controls confirmation if we move forward. Can you put together a first pass MAP with acceptance tests and owners by EOD?

Best,
Sana Patel
Head of Clinical Automation
MedSys Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval MAP + critical acceptance questions

Sana — thanks for the clear asks. Draft MAP attached (MAP-draft-v1.pdf). High-level summary below; full detail in the PDF and the shared Drive link.

Quick summary of success signals (measurable, owner, threshold):
- Latency: p95 < 350ms for inference on typical 512-token prompts — owner: Redwood infra (Ben) — daily sample.
- Throughput: sustained 40 reqs/min under typical batching profile during peak window — owner: MedSys / Redwood SRE (joint).
- Clinical concordance: 92% of model suggestions match clinician-validated answers on a 200-item test set (see test harness) — owner: MedSys clinical lead.
- Safety regression: zero high-severity hallucinations in 1,000 sampled responses (manual review) — owner: MedSys safety reviewer.

Exit gates / tie-breakers (examples):
- Fail fast: If latency p95 > 600ms for two consecutive days despite suggested tuning, escalate and pause live routing.
- Data-loss event: Any evidence of message logs missing for >24 hours triggers immediate suspension and root-cause evidence.
- Quality fail: If concordance drops below 85% in two rolling weekly samples, we’ll execute the rollback plan.

Acceptance test examples (automated + manual):
- Smoke: basic API health, KV cache correctness, sample prompt/response sanity (owner: Redwood SRE).
- Regression suite: 200 curated prompts, automated scoring against ground truth (owner: Redwood QA / MedSys clinical lead).
- Load: 30-minute soak at projected peak with cost/latency telemetry capture (owner: Ben).

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa will add the concrete test owners and the exact evaluation scripts.
2) We’ll align on evidence artifacts (logs, console exports, SOC2 snapshot) for procurement.
3) Formalize the week-by-week timeline in the shared Drive doc.

I've attached the draft MAP and linked the working doc. Marissa / Ben — can you review acceptance tests and add owners by 3pm PT?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (application/pdf)
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/medsys/MAP-v1

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval MAP + critical acceptance questions

Hannah — adding the acceptance-test granularity and owners below (copying what I’ll drop into the MAP PDF).

Acceptance test catalog (owner / run cadence / evidence artifact):
- Smoke API check (Ben) — run on every deploy and once daily during pilot. Evidence: healthcheck log excerpt + tracer id list.
- Latency sampling (Ben) — hourly p95 + sample traces for any p95 > 350ms. Evidence: CSV telemetry export + a link to the trace in Sentry/Tracing.
- Regression scoring (Marissa / MedSys clinical lead) — run nightly on the 200-item canonical set. Evidence: scoring report (CSV) + confusion matrix.
- Hallucination triage (MedSys safety reviewer) — weekly manual review of 250 random outputs; classify severity. Evidence: annotated spreadsheet + examples.
- Data retention spot-check (Redwood compliance) — weekly verification of log retention window and access controls. Evidence: export of retention policy + signed attestation.

Smoke checklist (sample items):
- Auth & rate limit behave as expected for pilot keys.
- KV cache warmup present after restart within 2 minutes.
- No >5% token failure rate on sample corpus.

Rollback plan (brief):
- Tier 1: Auto-fallback to smaller model variant + alert; 30-minute mitigation window.
- Tier 2: Pause routing; scale down to test traffic only; replicate issue in staging.
- Tier 3: Full rollback to pre-pilot baseline and schedule incident review.

I added test-run templates and a small script for nightly scoring into the Drive folder. Ben — I left the load-script for you to confirm.

-marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood

- Procurement needs explicit language confirming: logs (inference requests/responses) will be retained for 90 days for audit and will not be used to train models without written consent. Can you point us to the exact artifact/evidence we can rely on?
- For the clinical concordance test: can you share the scoring rubric you’ll use so our clinical team can sanity-check it?

If those two items are explicit in the MAP, we can approve and route to procurement. Attaching procurement requirements for reference.

Sana

Sana — good questions. Short answers and artifacts:

- Retention & training: Redwood will retain inference logs (request metadata + responses) for 90 days in the pilot environment. We will not persist training datasets derived from your production data and will not use any pilot data to retrain models without an explicit SOW. Evidence: 1) exportable retention policy PDF (attached in Drive), 2) a signed SOC 2 snapshot (we’ll provide the relevant pages), 3) a sample console export (CSV) showing retention timestamps.

- Scoring rubric: I uploaded the clinical concordance rubric to the Drive (tab "rubric-v1"). High-level: each sample is graded pass/partial/fail with defined acceptance thresholds per category (clinical fact, recommendation, contraindication). We’ll run nightly scoring and share the automated report; manual adjudication for borderline cases.

Next steps: I’ll update the MAP PDF with explicit procurement language and the rubric link, then share the Drive link for final sign-off. If procurement is happy, we can execute the mutual action plan and kick off the pilot on Mon 9/8.

Thanks everyone — looping Ben and Marissa to confirm the load test window and the SOC 2 pages we’ll export.

— Hannah
